name: How long does it take to build an ADU bathroom?

mainEntity.name: How many days or weeks does an ADU bathroom take from rough plumbing to final finishes?
mainEntity.text: How many days or weeks does an ADU bathroom take from rough plumbing to final finishes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The active build time for an ADU bathroom may be short, but the full schedule is often longer than homeowners expect because several steps must happen in sequence. Rough plumbing, electrical, framing, and inspection usually come first. Waterproofing and tile work follow, and those materials need proper drying and cure time before fixtures can be installed. Custom vanities, specialty tile, glass shower enclosures, or backordered fixtures can add more time. In Los Angeles-area projects, the permit and inspection schedule can also affect the calendar, especially if the bathroom layout changes during plan check. If the bathroom is part of a garage conversion or detached ADU, timing may depend on how fast the contractor can complete trenching, sewer tie-in, and utility coordination. A realistic schedule should include extra time for corrections, field changes, and final punch-list work. Homeowners should ask for a sequence that shows rough-in, inspection, waterproofing, tile, fixture installation, and final approval separately so delays are easier to manage.
acceptedAnswer.description: A basic ADU bathroom can take a few weeks of active construction, but the full timeline is usually longer because plumbing, inspections, waterproofing, tile curing, and finish work happen in stages. Delays often come from permit reviews, inspection scheduling, fixture lead times, and changes to the drain or vent layout.
